You can grow onions from scraps (I just pulled up 7 onions from two scraps), potatoes, celery and use carrot tops to grow carrot greens. The greens are nutritious, but many people are allergic I guess. Carrot tops have kind of an earthier minty taste, almost like cilantro. Aside from potatoes, I start the scraps in little cups of water until the roots grow a few inches then plant.

For onions, cut the greens back after planting, and plant very shallow (a little bit of the bulb peeking above the dirt). They're ready when the greens fall over on the ground, and just pull them up. Not sure how celery will do once planted, mine were eaten by something :(

If you do potatoes, once the pant gets about 6" tall, start mounding the plant with dirt, and do so every few inches of growth. This will protect the potatoes from the sun - green potatoes can be toxic.

I've also grown bell peppers from grocery store peppers, haven't tried jalapenos yet.

I just potted some celery that was grown from scrap.

Just cut off the bottom (where all of the stalks are attached - leave arm inch or two), plop it into a shallow bowl of water until new growth is seen (will start in the center), then plant.
